newsitem.title: UK: Mideast tanker rates unmoved by U.S. Iraqi strike.
newsitem.headline: Mideast tanker rates unmoved by U.S. Iraqi strike.

text.p: Middle East VLCC spot tanker rates on Tuesday failed to budge despite escalating tension in the region following a U.S. military strike against Iraq.
VLCC rates stayed at the lower levels established in the middle of last week, although chartering activity increased in a busier market, brokers said.
VLCCs travelling to Japan remained at W65 with western voyages still only able to command approximately W55.
Idemitsu's chartering of the 250,000 tonne cargo on the Diamond Falcon, heading for Japan at W64.5 was seen typical of the market.
After relative inactivity the previous day, coinciding with the U.S Labor Day holiday, three VLCCs were seen heading Eastwards along with several LR2 vessels.
"We estimate there to be roughly 94 VLCCs to be fixed between now and early October, and consequently there is a likelihood that rates will take on an upwards bias soon," said a broker.
Mediterranean 80,000 tonners lost further ground amid poor chartering, descending to W95 from previous levels of W98.
In the inter-UKC sector rates on 80,000 tonners took a tumble from W100 to W95 as evidenced in Chevron's chartering of the Saint Concertina.
The Caribbean saw rates settle around last done levels.
By the close of the day no fresh fixtures had been reported. Brokers explained that this was primarily due to the tail end of Monday's U.S Holiday.
Vessels of 70,000 tonnes travelling up the U.S coast still were commanding rates of W130.
West African rates consolidated amid poor chartering to the U.S and the East.
Suezmaxes to the U.S sustained levels of W86 to W88.
